hero.subtitle: Engineering & Craft in the Heart of Nicosia
hero.lede: Inside the Venetian walls, in a workshop of golden sandstone, we take apart the machine behind every cup — piece by piece.
hero.canvasLabel: A walnut-panelled espresso machine pulling a fresh golden shot and pouring it over crystal ice as you scroll.

ritual.heroLede: Inside Nicosia's Venetian walls, in a workshop of golden limestone — scroll naturally to experience the entire ritual from 9-bar extraction to the amber pour over crystal ice.
ritual.originsLede: Behind the fresh glass lifted from the group head stand three seasonal signature origins.

ready.caption: PID-locked at 93.0 °C, the brass group head and hand-turned walnut portafilter stand ready for the first drop.

extraction.caption: Under 9 bars of pressure, 18 g of freshly roasted coffee yields a dense, hazelnut-striped crema.

craft.caption: At 28 seconds and 36 g yield, the double ristretto is lifted warm toward crystal-clear ice.

pour.caption: 93 °C meets 4 °C in an instant thermal shift — locking dark chocolate and citrus into ribbons of amber.

pour.title: From 93 °C to 4 °C — alchemy over crystal ice.
pour.body: The instant a fresh double ristretto meets crystal ice, volatile aromatics lock in — cascading into ribbons of mahogany, dark chocolate and citrus.

boiler.title: Copper Heat-Exchange Boiler & PID Thermal Precision
boiler.body: A thick-walled copper boiler holds heat the way old stone does. A PID controller samples dozens of times a second, so temperature never drifts from one cup to the next.

groups.title: Triple E61 Brass Group Heads & Hand-Turned Walnut Portafilters
groups.body: Four kilos of thermosiphon-heated brass carry water evenly from the very first drop. The walnut handles are turned one by one on a Nicosia craftsman's lathe.

pump.title: Rotary Vane Pump & 9‑Bar Extraction Profiling
pump.body: A near-silent rotary vane pump shapes pressure like a breath — pre-infusion, peak, decline. Every coffee gets its own curve.

callouts.outro: Not the sum of the parts — the care between them.

manifesto.p1: The yellow sandstone of the walled city has been storing sunlight for centuries; at dusk it is still warm to the palm. That is how we like our coffee: unhurried, holding its heat.
manifesto.p2: In our workshop, stainless steel works beneath five-hundred-year-old arches. On one side: scales, probes, profile curves. On the other: scent, sound, intuition. They share the same bench.

roasts.title: Three origins, three temperaments.
roasts.lede: Three signatures chosen from the season's finest lots. Keep scrolling to move through them.

espresso.name: Espresso
espresso.body: Nine bar, eighteen grams, thirty seconds. Russet crema, a finish of dark chocolate.

pourover.name: Pour-Over
pourover.body: Slow pours through V60 and Kalita Wave. Floral, tea-like, a cup that opens in layers.

coldbrew.name: Cold Brew
coldbrew.body: Sixteen hours steeped in cold water — the coolest shade in Nicosia on an August afternoon.

cezve.name: Cypriot Coffee
cezve.body: Brewed in a copper cezve over hot sand, its foam gathered with patience. The workshop's oldest recipe.

cta.title: We roast on Thursdays. The scent drifts all the way to the Arasta.

menu.title: Nicosia in a glass
menu.lede: Carob from the island, pistachio from Antep, flowers from Ethiopia. Our menu is below — and beneath it, a calculator to build the same cup at home.

calc.title: Find the ratio, build the cup.

tips.pourover: Bloom with the first 50 g of water for 40 seconds, then pour slowly in spirals from the centre outward.
tips.espresso: Flow should begin around seconds 6–8. If it arrives early, grind one step finer.
tips.coldbrew: Steep in the fridge, strain through paper, dilute 1:1 with water and serve over ice.

team.title: The hands behind the cup
team.lede: Four people, one roaster, one stone counter. In the narrowest street of Nicosia we ask the same question every day: could this cup be better?

about.title: The second life of a stone workshop
about.lede: In a back street of the Arasta stood a blacksmith's workshop, its door locked for decades. The arches were sound, the walls were yellow sandstone, the ceiling a home for swallows.

story.p1: When we took the key in the winter of 2019, we found an anvil, a bellows and fifty years of silence. It took eleven months to free the walls from plaster and let the stone show its own colour.
story.p2: The blacksmith's hearth now houses the flue of our roaster. Same fire; we simply forge coffee instead of iron.
story.quote: The walls were built to protect the city. We are here to protect the small things inside it: the first scent of morning, a neighbour's greeting, the quiet of a good cup.

philosophy.title: Small batches, close attention.
philosophy.p1: Every batch on our 12-kilo, Loring-style convection roaster gets its own profile. Our Probat drum carries the round, syrupy body of our espresso blends.
philosophy.p2: We log every batch, verify it with colour measurement and approve it in a blind cupping the next morning. A batch we don't love never goes on sale.

points.b: Agtron colour reading for every batch

sustain.title: At the same table as the grower.
sustain.p1: We buy 80% of our coffee directly from producers, with no intermediaries — paying for quality, not the commodity index. You can trace every sack back to its farm.
sustain.p2: Spent grounds become compost for two community gardens in Nicosia; the jute sacks are sewn into bags by a local workshop.

contact.title: A stone door inside the walls.
contact.lede: Walk from the shadow of the Selimiye towards the Arasta; the scent of roasting will lead you the rest of the way.
